title: New Zealand to give duty-free access to Bangladesh post LDC graduation
summary:
New Zealand is keen on continuing duty-free and preferential market access facilities for Bangladesh even after the country’s LDC graduation, the former’s non-resident high commissioner to the latter David Pine said. 
Both sides discussed ways to further expand bilateral trade and investment ties, make use of existing regional trade frameworks and the possibility of signing a comprehensive bilateral FTA.

title: India-EU FTA to be implemented by 2026 end: European Commission prez
summary:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen recently vowed to implement the India-EU FTA by 2026 end, announcing to make the deal ‘fully operational at record speed’. 
The moment will be marked by a business event for European and Indian firms, she said in Gothenburg. 
Indian PM Modi invited European industry leaders to partner with India in digital infrastructure, AI and clean energy.

title: India reimposes polyester yarn QCO after Gujarat HC stay
summary:
India has reimposed Quality Control Order (QCO) compliance on polyester yarn imports after the Gujarat High Court stayed the withdrawal of QCOs for FDY, POY and DTY.
The move is expected to support domestic producers through tighter import checks, while increasing compliance costs and creating supply concerns for downstream textile industries dependent on imported yarn.

title: India, Netherlands to raise bilateral trade, market access, investment
summary:
India and the Netherlands have agreed to raise bilateral trade, market access and investment, especially in high-potential sectors like textiles, renewable energy, infrastructure and organic chemicals. 
This will be done through joint ventures, industrial partnerships and tech collaboration between companies from both sides. 
Both agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a strategic partnership.

title: Polyester yarn prices rise in India on firmer feedstock costs
summary:
Polyester yarn prices in India moved higher, supported by stronger PTA, MEG and melt costs that prompted producers to raise POY, DTY, PTY and FDY prices.
Despite soft and volatile crude oil trends, higher feedstock costs, tighter availability in some segments and import pressures supported the uptrend, with sentiment expected to remain firm if raw material costs stay elevated.

title: LYCRA to launch ADAPTIV fibre for nonwovens at INDEX 26
summary:
The LYCRA Company will launch LYCRA ADAPTIV fibre for nonwovens at INDEX 26, targeting diapers, hygiene, adult incontinence and feminine care. 
The fibre offers adaptive stretch, improved fit, comfort in motion, leakage protection, easier donning and doffing, inclusive sizing and fewer skin marks. 
It is also nominated for the INDEX Award in raw materials.

title: Turkiye’s current account deficit expected to widen in 2026: Minister
summary:
Turkiye recorded a current account deficit (CAD) of $9.6 billion in March, the country’s central bank said. 
Treasury and Finance Minister Mehmet Simsek said the CAD is expected to widen this year, due to high energy and non-energy commodity prices. 
Simsek said the deterioration is likely to remain temporary and manageable, thanks to stronger macroeconomic fundamentals and policy gains.

title: Vietnam’s FDI sector contributes over 20% of GDP: Deputy PM
summary:
Vietnam’s FDI sector contributes more than a fifth of the GDP, accounting for around seven-tenths of the export turnover, Deputy PM Nguyen Van Thang said. 
Amid falling global FDI flows into several regions, Vietnam continues as a leading FDI destination in ASEAN, he said. 
Nguyen said Vietnam will continue promoting institutional reforms and improving the investment and business environment.

title: Inflation cuts deep into consumer spending in Bangladesh: DCCI index
summary:
High inflation is cutting deep into Bangladesh consumer spending, with weak demand turning one of the biggest concerns for businesses, DCCI said. 
Higher rents, utility bills and fuel prices are eating away at already thin profit margins. 
DCCI’s economic position index revealed that consumers have sharply reduced spending as the cost of living continues to rise. 
SMEs are feeling the pressure the most.

title: EU green mandates and the Vietnam T&A industry
summary:
Vietnam’s textile and footwear exporters are accelerating sustainability efforts as stricter EU regulations reshape market access requirements. 
Rising compliance pressure from measures such as CBAM and ESPR is pushing manufacturers toward circular production, cleaner technologies and greater supply-chain transparency, though limited green finance remains a major challenge for smaller firms.

title: US’ Aramark’s Q2 revenue grows on US, international gains
summary:
Aramark has reported revenue of $4.9 billion in Q2 FY26, up 15 per cent YoY, driven by new business wins and growth across US and international operations. 
Operating income rose 26 per cent to $220 million, while adjusted EPS grew 40 per cent. 
Cash flow strengthened, client retention exceeded 98 per cent, and the company raised its organic revenue outlook.

title: Why Spring/Summer 2026 fashion colours reflect global chaos
summary:
Spring/Summer 2026 fashion is balancing bold and neutral palettes, with tomato red emerging as the standout colour alongside shades such as lost lilac, moody blue, soured citrus and jaded teal.  
Industry experts say earthy neutrals are becoming wardrobe foundations, while brighter tones are increasingly used as accents to add energy, nostalgia and emotional appeal.

title: South Korea’s Misto Holdings Q1 revenue rises 4.2% to $867.3 mn
summary:
Misto Holdings has reported a strong Q1 2026, with consolidated revenue rising 4.2 per cent YoY to KRW 1.3 trillion (~$867.3 million) and operating profit increasing 19 per cent to KRW 193.7 billion. 
Growth was driven by Acushnet, improved Misto profitability, China expansion, K-fashion momentum, and Fila product gains, despite macroeconomic uncertainty, tariffs and weak consumer sentiment.

title: Mandate govt garment procurement from Ghanaian producers: AGAM
summary:
The Association of Ghana Apparel Manufacturers (AGAM) recently called for a national procurement policy for garments and textiles, saying such a step may create over 100,000 jobs. 
If the government makes it compulsory for state institutions to procure uniforms and other garments from domestic manufacturers, the apparel sector can absorb thousands of unemployed youth, AGAM noted.

title: India’s PDS FY26 gross margin improves to 20.6%, GMV up 5%
summary:
PDS Limited has reported higher FY26 revenue and profit despite global trade and demand uncertainties. 
GMV rose 5 per cent YoY to ₹19,666 crore (~$2.04 billion), while consolidated topline grew 4 per cent to ₹13,110 crore (~$1.36 billion). 
PAT stood at ₹178 crore (~$18.49 million), with gross margin improving to 20.6 per cent. 
The company also strengthened its cash flow and reduced debt.

title: Brazil’s apparel imports rise 19% amid growing reliance on China
summary:
Brazil’s apparel imports rose 19 per cent year-on-year to $833.75 million in Q1 2026, driven mainly by strong demand for man-made fibre and knitwear products.
China further strengthened its dominance, supplying over 60 per cent of imports, highlighting Brazil’s growing dependence on Chinese sourcing despite global diversification efforts.

title: Rising costs push Sri Lankan apparel SMEs to the edge
summary:
Sri Lanka’s apparel industry is facing mounting pressure as exports reportedly fell around 8 per cent in Q1 2026 amid weak global demand, rising fuel and electricity costs, shipping disruptions and geopolitical uncertainty. 
Smaller manufacturers are being hit hardest, with industry bodies urging urgent policy support, energy reforms and stronger trade access to stabilise the sector.

title: UK’s clothing exports dip 7.8% to $884 mn in January-March 2026
summary:
United Kingdom clothing exports declined 7.87 per cent year-on-year to £655 million in January–March 2026, while textile fabric and fibre exports also weakened, according to Office for National Statistics data.
The fall reflected subdued demand in key European markets, cost pressures, and geopolitical uncertainties, although fibre shipments showed slight sequential improvement from Q4 2025.

title: Nigeria Kwara Garment Factory, KWS Garment Production Village ink pact
summary:
Nigerian state-run Kwara Garment Factory has signed a pact agreement with KWS Garment Production Village, allowing the latter to manage and run the former. 
A minimum of 80 per cent of the factory’s production workforce will be women and indigenes of Kwara state. 
The management model has been carefully structured to protect the state’s investment while allowing private sector excellence to thrive.

title: UK’s clothing imports fall 3% in Q1, sharply lower than Q4 2025
summary:
UK’s clothing imports declined 3.04 per cent year-on-year to £3.95 billion during January–March 2026, while textile fabric imports also edged lower, according to Office for National Statistics data.
March clothing imports fell 6.34 per cent from a year earlier.
The figures reflected softer apparel demand after the UK recorded moderate import growth in 2025 following a sharp decline in 2023.
